summary: The note describes the New York Yankees, an MLB team in the AL East based in the Bronx, and its origins as the Baltimore Orioles in 1901, then the New York Highlanders, renamed the Yankees in 1913. It also covers the 2009 season, when the team opened the new Yankee Stadium and won its 27th World Series title over the Philadelphia Phillies.
one_line: Overview of the New York Yankees, from their 1901 origins as the Baltimore Orioles to the 2009 World Series title, their 27th.
key_facts: The New York Yankees are an American professional baseball team based in the Bronx, New York City.
The Yankees compete in Major League Baseball as a member of the American League East division.
The New York Mets of the National League are the other major league club based in New York City.
The club began play in the AL in 1901 as the Baltimore Orioles, which has no relation to the modern Baltimore Orioles.
Frank Farrell and Bill Devery purchased the franchise, which had ceased operations, moved it to New York City, and renamed it the New York Highlanders.
The Highlanders were officially renamed the Yankees in 1913.
Before the 2009 season the Yankees signed star free agents including CC Sabathia, Mark Teixeira, and A.J. Burnett.
The new Yankee Stadium opened at the start of the 2009 season, a block north on River Avenue from the former stadium.
The Yankees set a major league record by playing error-free ball for 18 consecutive games from May 14 to June 1, 2009.
In 2009 the Yankees finished first in the AL East, swept the Twins in the ALDS, and beat the Angels in six games in the ALCS.
The Yankees beat the defending champion Philadelphia Phillies in Game 6 of the World Series 7-3, winning the series 4-2.
The 2009 World Series was the Yankees' 27th World Series title.
